subtext: Built, rebuilt and tested by engineers who work on Land Rover engines every day.
Here's our practical view of the 200Tdi across its Land Rover applications.

columns.title: APPLICATIONS WE SEE:
columns.body: The 200Tdi is a classic Land Rover engine, fitted to the Defender L316 from 1990 to 1994. It's one of the simpler and more robust Land Rover diesel engines we work on.

columns.title: WHAT WE REPLACE:
columns.body: Timing belt, tensioner, VE injection pump, head gasket, bearings, and gaskets as standard on every rebuild.

columns.title: KNOWN ISSUES:
columns.body: Timing belt failure (the 200Tdi is an interference engine — belt failure causes valve-to-piston contact), VE fuel injection pump leaks, head gasket failure, and fuel system issues including lumpy idle and stalling.

notice.rest: engine-specific case studies with real job details are not yet included on this page — they'll be added once a documented set of completed 200Tdi rebuilds is available to draw from, rather than filled with placeholder examples now.

typical.title: LAND ROVER 200Tdi REBUILD
typical.intro: The following describes a typical rebuild scope for this engine — illustrative of the work involved, not a specific customer job. Real case studies from our own completed work will replace this section once available.
typical.body: The 200Tdi is one of the simpler diesel engines we work on — it uses mechanical fuel injection rather than common-rail, which means no high-pressure injector pump or complex electronic management to recalibrate. The engine's simplicity means a full rebuild is more straightforward than many of the later, more complex engines in the Land Rover range.

scope.label: Typical Scope:
scope.text: Timing belt, tensioner, injection pump, head gasket, bearings, gaskets
